title: Cost Compass: Initiative Tracker for Batching, Caching, and Quantization
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary: Cost Compass is a cross-functional initiative to deliver a prioritized, measurable program that reduces inference unit economics by optimizing batching, prefix/KV caching, and aggressive-but-safe quantization profiles. The tracker aligns PM, Eng, and Design on experiments, canary rollouts, gating criteria, and dashboards needed to ship sustainable 12-20% cost savings for selected workloads while preserving quality and latency SLOs.

Objectives: Reduce per-token cost for tail and common workloads; establish reliable rollout and rollback gates; create an observability baseline and an experiment-to-rollout path.

Success metrics: 1) 15% median token cost reduction across target workloads within 90 days of rollout. 2) P95 latency regression <= 3% vs baseline. 3) Model output quality regressions (eval suites) within pre-approved thresholds (BLEU/ROUGE/semantic similarity deltas < 1.5% for targeted tasks). 4) Field adoption: 60% of eligible routes using adaptive serving knobs after Q2.

Scope: experiments on continuous batching heuristics and dynamic batch-sizing, prefix/KV cache TTL policies and eviction strategies, and per-workload quantization profiles (int8 + selective mixed-precision). Includes console UX to expose recommendations and rollout controls, plus automated rollback and alerting for quality regressions.

M4: Quantization safety lanes and per-model profile library published - 2026-05-05
M5: Canary rollouts with automatic rollback and cost dashboards - 2026-05-28
M6: Full soft-rollout and adoption playbook published - 2026-06-30
experiment_plan: Batching experiments: constant vs adaptive batch sizing; evaluate throughput, tail latency, and unit cost at 1%, 10%, 50% traffic mixes.
KV cache experiments: TTL sweep (200ms to 10s), prefix-match policies, per-customer cache shards; monitor cache hit uplift and downstream token savings.
Quantization experiments: evaluate int8 and 4-bit safe paths vs fp16 baseline on three model families; include eval suites and synthetic adversarial prompts.
Traffic shaping trials: canary low-latency lanes preserved while routing non-critical traffic to thrift profiles for max savings.
A/B quality gating: automated eval run per deploy; block rollout if quality delta exceeds threshold or if customer-reported complaints spike by 25%.
Cost modeling: integrate experiment telemetry into econ dashboard to show projected annualized savings and per-route ROI.
acceptance_criteria: Backfilled baseline metrics for target routes (cost per token, p50/p95 latency, quality scores)
Experiment harness producing reproducible scorecards and automated report generation
Canary pipeline that can do 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% progression with rollback hooks
Console UI for rollout controls and visibility to cost impact per-route
Runbook describing rollback thresholds, incident playbook, and customer comms template
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Quantization causes subtle quality regressions in rare prompts. Mitigation: require multi-metric eval and human-in-loop signoff for production rollouts.
Risk: Cache eviction policies introduce flapping across models. Mitigation: staged TTL increases and per-model observability with anomaly alerts.
Risk: Batching increases tail latency for latency-sensitive customers. Mitigation: preserve low-latency lane and shape traffic into thrift lane only for non-critical routes.
Risk: Insufficient telemetry granularity. Mitigation: add per-token tagging and sample traces for 1% of requests during experiments.
